tex_content.html: \begin{exercise} \end{exercise} 1. ch12:12-2↗ ex:real-projective-space-metric Prove that if $n$ is even, then every orientation-preserving orthogonal linear map from $\mathbb {R}^{n+1}$ to itself fixes at least one point of the unit sphere, and use this to prove that every even-dimensional spherical space form is isometric to either a round sphere or a real projective space with a constant multiple of the metric defined in Example 2.34. (Used on p. 349.) \end{exercise}
